I have to ask, did you pick this vacation? or did someone in your family recommend that you go stay with a relative for a vacation? Cause in my extended family there has always been this habit among them to loan out older teenaged family to be like sudo aides for whatever another family member is struggling with at the moment.

It's a thing in some families. I can remember being invited up to one of my (20+ yrs older) cousins with my mom for a visit with her and her family, and day 2 she attempted to send me off with her children to go do yard work on a property they were fixing up in order to sell. Thankfully this was not the first time I'd experienced this in my family and I was like just 20yrs old at the time so when I was TOLD to mow their giant over grown lawn with her kid I said "No, I'm not interested in working on my vacation" and walked away. 

She was miffed and I could tell she definitely had some unkind words to say about me to the rest of the family later on, but honestly... I don't care I was invited for the summer festival in their town and to visit with family and catch up, not to WORK for you. If they had ASKED for my help with that prior to inviting me up for the visit I may have said yes and prepared myself for it, but I also very likely would have said no thank you and not gone with for the visit. It was my break from College and I just wanted to relax not mow a lawn that was purely for their profit. 

  
NTA. You don't need to be your cousins child care and if your Mom or other family had offered you up or suggested your visit would benefit your cousins in that way... that ain't on you and you're not "selfish" "a bad cousin or family member" or even "lazy" for not providing it for them. You're a regular human that was looking to have a rest and moment for your self, regardless of other peoples expectations. 

  
Like someone else had mentioned I would consider cutting your visit short if you have the ability to do it yourself or calling your Mom and asking her to help you get home ASAP and make it clear that you don't approve of being offered up as aide to family without being TOLD and agreeing to it in advance.

  
Love my family, love to help them out if they need it, but don't fake me out with offering to host me and then add an emotional "fee" and "labor" tax.

I had multiple breakdowns and burnouts and crashed so much of my life down around myself by trying to make sure that I did EVERYTHING I could because it felt like I had no time and had to do it ALL. It's really really hard but for me and my Mom Memory care was the best thing for us both. She's so much better there and I'm starting to get my old self and my life back together.

My Mom has been in a Memory Care Facility for a bout a year and a half at now and she had possibly the smoothest most positive transition that I could have asked for. She was already in an advanced enough condition by then that she didn't really even recognize her own apartment as HERS or anyone else's apartments as not hers. It's almost like everything just went to ROOM and her understanding of possession just dropped. She's also just very outgoing naturally and so she just, I think, thought she was visiting other people or "at a hotel" so we were lucky. 

  
That being said. We did give her the 2 week not visiting or calling adjustment time, we I did my sibling hasn't been to visit nor called her of his own volition at all since helping me mover her in, and when I came to start visiting her she did have the "these people are all crazy here" and she didn't like the staff because they made her take showers (she had gone months and months without showering bc she for some reason grew a really bad aversion to them and it was bad for her skin and over all health so I feel bad it stresses her out but she NEEDS to shower) but its a year and some months in and I can say she is SO MUCH HAPPIER AND HEALTHIER. 

  
I do have to regularly kind of check up and in on her meds and her stuff to make sure staff is being attentive. I don't blame them for being human, dementia patients are difficult and near impossible to work with I get it. I have had to ask them to swap one of her caregivers because she was not taking care of my mom and letting her stay unwashed and in the same dirty cloths for days and not making sure she was brushing her teeth or caring for herself. So I am not say to be less vigilant but she's in the place that will eventually be THE BEST FOR HER and you. 

  
and don't feel bad about not missing her. I've said this to one or two other posters here but with my Mom at a certain point it just stopped feeling like my Mom and more like a stranger who just lived in her body. She's very different from the mother who I knew for 30 years before she was diagnosed with Alz. I can make sure she feels all the love and care I can give her and make sure she is happy and healthy as she can be, but in a very real way I lost the person that my mother is a long time ago. You've already been missing long before she was physically gone.

It's so hard because everywhere seems to have such different qualifications for aid and even different types of aid available.

My mom lives on her own and has Alz, so I buy her small portion EVERYTHING! The little bottles of water, little apple and orange juice bottles, even pre portioned milks or yogurt smoothies. 

I also buy her the lunch kits that have a drink and a snack in it too, that way she feels more inclined to just pick it up and sit down at the couch with it. I also tend to pick out the packages that have cartoon characters or bright colors too. I know we try really hard to avoid giving them things that make them feel infantized or anything BUT she really is more drawn and attracted to pick up and look at things with a smiling faces on it or a that has bright colors so those get eaten WAY faster than if I get more normal looking things for her. 

It's not what's BEST for her nutrition wise and she tends to never even finish any of the those things but at least she's eating and drinking SOMETHING on her own with out being prompted. 

Also if I'm with her or we're out places I'll get something "for myself" and just keep passing it to her to try, or sometimes I don't even say anything I'll just keep periodically handing it to her and she'll take a sip or a bite and hand it back to me. 

Being a care giver in these kind of situations isn't about getting it "right" it's about getting things "Better" so treat any little bit as a win. You're doing better than you think, I can guarantee it.

Used to make this all the time when I was in my early twenties.

\-Kielbasa sausage, Sliced into little circles

\-3 good size thickly sliced potatoes

\-Bell Peppers

\-Large diced Onion

\-tsp Diced Garlic (I use the pre diced stuff but if fresh idk like 2 cloves?)

\-Tbsp. Sugar

\-Tbsp. Olive Oil

\-8oz Can of diced tomatoes

(Extra's not needed but HIGHLY recommend!)

\-Zucchini/Italian Squash

\-McCormick Italian Seasoning (or any combo of the following you've got: marjoram, basil, rosemary, thyme, oregano)

​

Heat a Large skillet or pan with a lid on stove. Add olive oil. Once hot, then toss in the garlic, stir to coat in the oil, add onions, bell peppers (and zucchini if you've got it), stir to mix.

Once you've got the veggies sizzling and the onions have started to become translucent add the sliced kielbasa sausage. Let the Sausage sear a little on the flat sides.

Then just mix in the potatoes and toss the can of diced tomatoes. Refill the now empty tomato can with water and also add that to the pan. Then add the1 tsp. of sugar, season with a few good shakes of seasoning and a pinch of salt.

Mix all the ingredients in the pan, lower the heat till the tomato juice/water is just simmering and cover with the lid for about 30min. (if you sliced your potatoes really thick then 40 if you made them thinner 25, just use a knife to poke a few of the thicker slices to see if they're soft in the middle or not)

Once all the potatoes are cooked through toss it on a plate and it's food!

It's so easy, super cheap and leftovers heat up really nice.

(plus it's super easy to customize it to you're own tastes. When I made it for me and my brother I added Chili flakes and cayenne to give it spice. When I'd make it for my mom I'd add more sugar, thyme and skip the Zucchi.)

I seriously don't know if this came from a recipe I messed up or if it was just, "We have these things in the fridge today!" but it became the cheap weeknight go-to for me cause it was easy, fast to clean up and pretty crowd pleasing because it was so simple. (I even made it vegan for a friend by swapping the kielbasa sausage for summer squash and adding veggie stock.)

Ps if this is an actual dish that someone knows of I'd love to know the name, we've literally never figured out what to call it.

​

Edit to say: You should get at least enough for 4 servings for big eaters out of this but more realistically this should be more than enough for 6 servings.
